page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-2 is an entry-tier, compute-leaning virtual machine instance from the N1 generation. It is provisioned with 2 vCPUs operating on a single physical core of an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, utilizing symmetric multithreading with two threads per core. System memory is sized at 2.0 GB, allocating approximately 0.9 GB of RAM per vCPU. The cache hierarchy includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and a 45 MB shared L3 cache. The CPU features baseline x86 vector and security extensions including AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, but lacks AVX-512 and matrix acceleration instructions. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark profiles reflect entry-level performance across compute and memory subsystems. In stress-ng evaluations, the instance produced a single-core score of 1,086.39 and a multi-core score of 1,408.88, situating it in the lower tiers of tested cloud instances. Memory throughput measured 80.82 GB/s for small cached blocks and 13.22 GB/s for large uncached 256 MB reads, alongside 11.3 GB/s on uncached write operations. PassMark CPU testing yielded an aggregate score of 1,638.85, with extended instructions scoring 1,158.92 and encryption reaching 652.65. Application-level benchmarks indicate throughput of 1.35 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 1.51 GB/s in static web serving, while small 135M parameter LLM inference achieved 65.68 prompt tokens per second and 38.74 generation tokens per second.

The primary constraint of the n1-highcpu-2 configuration is its narrow 2.0 GB memory envelope, which limits the density and scope of concurrent processes. Because persistent disk storage must be provisioned externally over the network, storage throughput is bounded by network interfaces rather than direct-attached media. From a resource-efficiency standpoint, the machine offers dedicated compute threads at lower resource commitments, avoiding the overhead of unused memory. It is appropriate for non-demanding compute tasks, lightweight message queues, background processing workers, simple HTTP proxies, and low-scale API microservices where data fits easily within restricted memory thresholds.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-2 is a compute-skewed virtual machine within the legacy N1 family. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, paired with 2.0 GB of system memory (0.9 GB per vCPU). The instance includes no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached persistent storage for persistence. In synthetic evaluations, the server demonstrates baseline compute and memory capabilities, registering a stress-ng multi-core score of 1,408.88 and 13.22 GB/s large-block read bandwidth. Cryptographic and bit-manipulation extensions such as AES, AVX, BMI2, and FMA are supported, while AVX-512 and AMX instructions are absent. Given the constrained memory allocation and entry-level execution metrics, this instance is suited for lightweight compute tasks, small-scale microservices, asynchronous worker queues, and basic utility scripts that do not require substantial memory arrays.
